name: Poland

income_tax.summary: Resident income tax is 12% on income up to PLN 120,000 (tax-free amount PLN 30,000, delivered as a PLN 3,600 tax-reducing amount) and PLN 10,800 plus 32% above that; a 4% solidarity levy applies above PLN 1,000,000. Employee contributions: 13.71% (pension and disability 11.26% up to the PLN 282,600 annual cap, sickness 2.45% uncapped) plus 9% health on income net of those contributions, uncapped. The recorded rate is the combined 22.71%; the cap applies to the 11.26% pension and disability part only.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Derived approximate rate on an income of about EUR 54,000 (about PLN 230,000 at an assumed ~4.25 PLN/EUR): fixed ZUS social contributions of PLN 1,870.24 a month (lower end, PLN 22,443 a year) plus 9% health on the tax scale (about PLN 18,700) is roughly PLN 41,100, i.e. about 17.9%. The fixed ZUS part does not scale with income; at EUR 130,000 (about PLN 550,000) the same components give roughly 12-13%. Statutory ZUS social contributions on the minimum base of PLN 5,652 a month are PLN 1,870.24-2,020.58 a month depending on the accident rate (33.09% of the base at the lower end). The pension and disability cap does not change the fixed base. Health, included in the recorded rate at the scale option: 9% of income (min PLN 432.54 a month from Feb 2026) on the tax scale, 4.9% of income on the 19% flat tax, and a fixed amount on ryczalt by annual revenue (PLN 498.35 to 60,000; 830.58 for 60,000-300,000; 1,495.04 above 300,000 on the PwC 2023 labels, which equal the 2026 figures quoted by a secondary source). A preferential ZUS on a PLN 1,441.80 base (PLN 441.76-480.11 a month) is available to new businesses. Business income: flat 19%, 14% for certain professions and 12% for designated IT services on lump-sum basis.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local income tax in the sources opened; the page does not cover local taxes. The 0% bracket from 0 to 30,000 stands in for the tax-free amount, so personal_allowance is 0.

2026 forecast average wage and PLN health amounts for ryczalt should be re-checked on zus.pl.

The 17.9% self-employed rate is derived (fixed ZUS plus 9% health on the scale, at an assumed PLN/EUR rate); the effective rate depends on the tax option chosen (scale, 19% linear with 4.9% health, or ryczalt with fixed health).

regimes.name: Ryczalt (lump-sum) for designated IT services
regimes.description: Self-employed contractors (B2B) can pay a revenue-based lump-sum tax instead of the scale. PwC states certain designated IT services pay 12%; the full rate schedule by activity was not opened. Costs cannot be deducted; health contribution is a fixed amount by annual revenue.

regimes.name: Linear 19% flat tax on business income
regimes.description: Sole traders may elect a flat 19% on business profit (after costs) instead of the 12%/32% scale; health is 4.9% of income. Certain professions pay 14%.

rent_1bed_monthly.description: Average asking rent for 40-59 m2 flats (Polish 'two-room', typically one bedroom plus living room), Otodom Analytics via Investropa, updated 4 Oct 2026; asking rents, unfurnished status not stated. Studios under 40 m2: PLN 2,976.

source.title: Warsaw rents 2026 (Otodom Analytics asking rents via Investropa)

rent_2bed_monthly.description: Average asking rent for 60-89 m2 flats in Warsaw (Polish 'three-room', typically two bedrooms plus living room), Otodom Analytics via Investropa, page updated 4 Oct 2026; +1.5% year on year; asking rents, city-wide (no city-centre split), furnished status not stated, sample size not stated. The 60-89 m2 band is wider than a strict 2-bedroom.

source.title: Warsaw rents 2026 (Otodom Analytics asking rents via Investropa)

costs.notes: The 2-bedroom figure is the Otodom 60-89 m2 size band, the closest published to a three-room flat; the page has no city-centre split (district averages: Wilanow ~PLN 5,500, Wola 4,300-4,500, Mokotow 4,300-4,400, sizes not stated). A blog (freenance.io, no method) listing city-centre 2-bedroom flats at PLN 5,000-7,500 was not used.

residence_routes: EU citizens may live and work freely and register their stay. US and other non-EU citizens need a visa and a work permit or a business route (sole trader or company); no remote-worker visa was found, and no official Polish page was opened for these routes, so the details are unverified. Skilled employees are normally sponsored by a Polish employer.
open_questions: Official Polish immigration route for non-EU contractors and employees not opened.
Ryczalt rate table by activity not opened.
2-bedroom rent is a 60-89 m2 band average, not a city-centre 2-bedroom median.
